title: ISO/IEC 22123-1:2023 — Cloud Computing Vocabulary — Scope
text:
ISO/IEC 22123-1:2023 Scope

This document provides the vocabulary for cloud computing. It establishes terms and definitions used across the ISO/IEC 22123 series and the broader ISO/IEC cloud computing standardisation programme. The vocabulary covers cloud computing concepts, cloud service categories, cloud capabilities types, cloud deployment models, cloud computing activities, cloud computing roles and sub-roles, functional components, cloud SLA terms, key characteristics, cross-cutting aspects, data terms, virtualisation concepts, multi-cloud concepts and physical organisation terms.

The ISO/IEC 22123 series consists of:
- ISO/IEC 22123-1: Vocabulary
- ISO/IEC 22123-2: Concepts
- ISO/IEC 22123-3: Reference architecture (CCRA)

title: Cloud computing — core terms
text:
Cloud computing core terms (Clause 3.1):

3.1.1 cloud: paradigm for enabling network access to a scalable and elastic pool of shareable physical or virtual resources with self-service provisioning and administration on-demand.
Note: Examples of resources include servers, operating systems, networks, software, applications and storage equipment.

3.1.2 cloud computing: paradigm for enabling network access to a scalable and elastic pool of shareable physical or virtual resources with self-service provisioning and administration on-demand.
Note: Cloud computing has five key characteristics: broad network access, measured service, on-demand self-service, rapid elasticity and resource pooling.

3.1.3 cloud service: one or more capabilities offered via cloud computing invoked using a defined interface.

3.1.4 cloud service customer data (CSC data): class of data objects under the control of the cloud service customer that were input by or for a cloud service customer through the use of a cloud service.

3.1.5 cloud service derived data: data generated by or from a cloud service provider's operations of a cloud service that results from interactions of the cloud service provider with the cloud service customer through the use of the cloud service.

3.1.6 cloud service provider data: class of data objects used by the cloud service provider that are either not provided by or for the cloud service customer, or are not cloud service customer data or cloud service derived data.

title: Cloud service categories
text:
Cloud service categories (Clause 3.2):

3.2.1 cloud service category: group of cloud services that possess some common set of qualities.

3.2.2 communications as a service (CaaS): cloud service category in which the capabilities provided to the cloud service customer are communications and collaboration.

3.2.3 compute as a service (CompaaS): cloud service category in which the capabilities provided to the cloud service customer are computational resources for operating cloud service customer applications.

3.2.4 data storage as a service (DSaaS): cloud service category in which the capabilities provided to the cloud service customer are data storage and related capabilities.

3.2.5 infrastructure as a service (IaaS): cloud service category in which the capabilities provided to the cloud service customer are processing, storage and other fundamental computing resources enabling the cloud service customer to deploy and run arbitrary software, which can include operating systems and applications.

3.2.6 network as a service (NaaS): cloud service category in which the capabilities provided to the cloud service customer are transport connectivity and related network capabilities.

3.2.7 platform as a service (PaaS): cloud service category in which the capabilities provided to the cloud service customer include deploying, managing and running cloud service customer-created or acquired applications using programming languages, libraries, services and tools supported by the cloud service provider.

3.2.8 software as a service (SaaS): cloud service category in which the capabilities provided to the cloud service customer are to use the cloud service provider's applications running on a cloud infrastructure.

title: Cloud capabilities types
text:
Cloud capabilities types (Clause 3.3):

3.3.1 cloud capabilities type: classification of the functionality provided by a cloud service to the cloud service customer as seen by the cloud service customer.

3.3.2 application capabilities type: cloud capabilities type in which the cloud service customer can use the cloud service provider's applications.

3.3.3 infrastructure capabilities type: cloud capabilities type in which the cloud service customer can provision and use processing, storage, networking and other fundamental computing resources.

3.3.4 platform capabilities type: cloud capabilities type in which the cloud service customer can deploy, manage and run cloud service customer-created or cloud service customer-acquired applications using programming languages, libraries, services and tools supported by the cloud service provider.

title: Cloud deployment models
text:
Cloud deployment models (Clause 3.4):

3.4.1 cloud deployment model: specific type of environment in which a cloud may be operated, identified according to access, ownership, size and purpose.

3.4.2 community cloud: cloud deployment model where the cloud infrastructure is provisioned for exclusive use by a specific community of cloud service customers from organisations that have shared concerns.
Note: Shared concerns may include mission, security requirements, policy and compliance considerations.

3.4.3 hybrid cloud: cloud deployment model using at least two different cloud deployment models.
Note: A hybrid cloud involves both private and public cloud or a combination including community cloud.

3.4.4 private cloud: cloud deployment model where the cloud infrastructure is provisioned for exclusive use by a single cloud service customer comprising one or more business units.
Note: The cloud infrastructure may be owned, managed and operated by the organisation, a third party, or some combination, and it may exist on or off premises.

3.4.5 public cloud: cloud deployment model where the cloud infrastructure is provisioned for open use by the general public.
Note: Public cloud infrastructure is owned, managed and operated by a business, academic or government organisation, or some combination.

3.4.6 multi-cloud: cloud deployment model using cloud services from more than one cloud service provider by a cloud service customer.

title: Cloud computing activities
text:
Cloud computing activities (Clause 3.5):

3.5.1 cloud computing activity: specified pursuit or set of tasks with an intent to achieve something from which cloud computing is a key element.
Note: Cloud computing activities need to have a purpose and deliver one or more outcomes.

3.5.2 use cloud service: cloud computing activity that involves a cloud service customer using the services of a cloud service provider to accomplish some tasks.
Note: The use cloud service activity typically involves the provision of user credentials to enable the CSP to authenticate the user and grant access, and the invocation of the cloud service which operates and delivers its specified outcomes.

title: Cloud computing roles and sub-roles
text:
Cloud computing roles and sub-roles (Clause 3.6):

3.6.1 cloud computing role: set of cloud computing activities associated with cloud computing.
Note: A party can play more than one role and can engage in a specific subset of activities of a role.

3.6.2 cloud service customer role (CSC role): cloud computing role that encompasses cloud computing activities for the purpose of using cloud services.

3.6.3 cloud service partner role (CSN role): cloud computing role that encompasses cloud computing activities in support of, or auxiliary to, activities of either the cloud service provider role or the cloud service customer role, or both.

3.6.4 cloud service provider role (CSP role): cloud computing role that encompasses cloud computing activities for the purpose of providing cloud services.

3.6.5 cloud computing sub-role: subdivision of a cloud computing role.
Note: Sub-roles are defined for the CSC role, CSP role and CSN role in ISO/IEC 22123-3.

CSC sub-roles:
3.6.6 CSC:cloud service administrator — sub-role responsible for administration of the tenancy, managing user accounts, security roles, identities and permissions; monitoring service quality; administering service security.
3.6.7 CSC:cloud service business manager — sub-role managing business aspects of using cloud services including procurement, financial management, billing.
3.6.8 CSC:cloud service user — sub-role that uses the cloud service to accomplish tasks.

CSP sub-roles:
3.6.9 CSP:cloud service operations manager — sub-role performing all operational processes ensuring services and infrastructure meet operational targets.
3.6.10 CSP:cloud service deployment manager — sub-role planning deployment of services into production.
3.6.11 CSP:cloud service manager — sub-role ensuring services are available for CSCs and function correctly per SLA.
3.6.12 CSP:cloud service business manager — sub-role managing business aspects of offering cloud services to CSCs.
3.6.13 CSP:customer support and care representative — sub-role managing customer interface and handling requests.
3.6.14 CSP:primary inter-cloud provider — sub-role relying on secondary CSPs to provide cloud services.
3.6.15 CSP:cloud service security and risk manager — sub-role ensuring appropriate management of risks associated with development, delivery, use and support of cloud services.
3.6.16 CSP:network provider — sub-role providing network connectivity and network services.

CSN sub-roles:
3.6.17 CSN:cloud service developer — sub-role designing, developing, testing and maintaining cloud service implementations.
3.6.18 CSN:cloud auditor — sub-role conducting audits of the provision and use of cloud services.
3.6.19 CSN:cloud service broker — sub-role negotiating relationships between cloud service customers and cloud service providers.

title: Functional components of the CCRA
text:
Functional components of the Cloud Computing Reference Architecture (Clause 3.7):

3.7.1 functional component: functional element of the cloud computing reference architecture (CCRA) which is used to perform an activity or some part of an activity and which has an implementation artefact in a concrete realisation of the architecture.

3.7.2 user layer: CCRA layer providing the user interface through which a cloud service customer role interacts with a cloud service provider role, performs customer administrative activities and monitors cloud services.

3.7.3 access layer: CCRA layer providing a common interface for both manual and automated access to the capabilities available in the services layer; responsible for authentication, authorisation and QoS enforcement.

3.7.4 service layer: CCRA layer containing the implementation of the services provided by a cloud service provider; contains and controls software components that implement the services.

3.7.5 resource layer: CCRA layer including equipment typically used in a data centre (servers, network switches, routers, storage devices) and corresponding non-cloud-specific software such as host operating systems, hypervisors, device drivers and generic systems management software.

3.7.6 multi-layer functions: CCRA functions that interact with functional components across all four layers; include operational support systems, business support systems, security systems, integration and development support capabilities.

title: Cloud SLA and service agreement terms
text:
Cloud SLA and service agreement terms (Clause 3.8):

3.8.1 cloud service agreement (CSA): agreement between a cloud service provider and a cloud service customer that covers all aspects of the cloud service relationship including service level, security, privacy and business terms.
Note: The CSA is the master agreement — the SLA is subservient to it.

3.8.2 cloud service level agreement (cloud SLA): service level agreement between a cloud service provider and a cloud service customer, based on a taxonomy of cloud computing specific terms, to set the quality of the cloud services delivered.
Note: The cloud SLA includes cloud service level objectives (SLOs) and cloud service qualitative objectives (SQOs). Defined in ISO/IEC 19086.

3.8.3 cloud service level objective (SLO): commitment made by a cloud service provider regarding a specific measurable characteristic of the cloud service.
Note: The cloud SLA includes all the cloud SLOs for the cloud service.

3.8.4 cloud service qualitative objective (SQO): qualitative commitment or description concerning the behaviour of a cloud service, not directly measurable but verifiable.

title: Key characteristics of cloud computing
text:
Key characteristics of cloud computing (Clause 3.9):

Cloud computing is characterised by five essential characteristics:

3.9.1 broad network access: characteristic where capabilities are available over the network and accessed through standard mechanisms that promote use by heterogeneous thin or thick client platforms (e.g. mobile phones, tablets, laptops, and workstations).

3.9.2 measured service: characteristic where cloud systems automatically control and optimise resource use by leveraging a metering capability at some level of abstraction appropriate to the type of service (e.g. storage, processing, bandwidth, and active user accounts); resource usage is monitored, controlled, and reported — providing transparency for both the provider and consumer of the utilised service.

3.9.3 on-demand self-service: characteristic enabling a cloud service customer to unilaterally provision computing capabilities, such as server time and network storage, as needed automatically without requiring human interaction with each service provider.

3.9.4 rapid elasticity: characteristic where capabilities can be elastically provisioned and released, in some cases automatically, to scale rapidly outward and inward commensurate with demand; to the consumer, the capabilities available for provisioning often appear to be unlimited and can be appropriated in any quantity at any time.

3.9.5 resource pooling: characteristic where the provider's computing resources are pooled to serve multiple consumers using a multi-tenant model, with different physical and virtual resources dynamically assigned and reassigned according to consumer demand.

title: Cross-cutting aspects of cloud computing
text:
Cross-cutting aspects of cloud computing (Clause 3.10):

Cross-cutting aspects are behaviours or capabilities coordinated across roles and implemented consistently in a cloud computing system.

3.10.1 auditability: capability of collecting and making available necessary evidential information related to the operation and use of a cloud service, for the purpose of conducting an audit.

3.10.2 availability: ability to be in a state to perform as required; depends upon combined characteristics of reliability, recoverability and maintainability. A key SLO in cloud SLAs.

3.10.3 governance: system by which the provision and use of cloud services are directed and controlled by the decision-makers of the organisation (CSP or CSC). Includes internal cloud governance (design-time and run-time policies) and external cloud governance (CSA and SLA obligations).

3.10.4 interoperability: ability of a cloud service customer's system to interact with a cloud service, or ability for one cloud service to interact with other cloud services, by exchanging information according to a prescribed method to obtain predictable results.

3.10.5 maintenance and versioning: process of modifying a system or component after delivery to correct flaws, improve performance or adapt to a changed environment. Versioning is the assignment of unique version identifiers to specific states of software configuration items.

3.10.6 performance: general term covering non-functional aspects of a cloud service including transaction rate, latency, throughput, concurrent service requests, storage capacity, concurrent execution threads, runtime memory and elasticity limits.

3.10.7 portability: ability to migrate applications (cloud application portability) or data (cloud data portability) from one cloud service to another, or between a cloud service customer's system and a cloud service.

3.10.8 protection of personally identifiable information (PII): appropriate collection, processing and disposal of PII. Governed by ISO/IEC 27701, ISO/IEC 27018 and ISO/IEC 29100. In cloud: CSC is typically PII controller, CSP is typically PII processor.

3.10.9 regulatory compliance: use and provision of cloud services is influenced by legal and regulatory provisions varying across jurisdictions. CSA and related SLA are core mechanisms for establishing compliance. Security and privacy governed by ISO/IEC 27017, 27018 and 27701.

3.10.10 resiliency: ability of a system to provide and maintain an acceptable level of service in the face of faults affecting normal operation; realised through monitoring, preventive and responsive processes including failover and redundancy.

3.10.11 reversibility: process for the cloud service customer to retrieve CSC data and application artefacts, and for the cloud service provider to delete all CSC data and cloud service derived data after an agreed period.

3.10.12 security: preservation of confidentiality, integrity and availability of information; also includes authenticity, accountability, non-repudiation and reliability. In cloud: shared responsibility between CSP and CSC depending on cloud service category. Governed by ISO/IEC 27017.

title: Cloud data terms
text:
Cloud data terms (Clause 3.11):

3.11.1 cloud service customer data (CSC data): class of data objects under the control of the cloud service customer that were input by or for a CSC through the use of a cloud service.

3.11.2 cloud service derived data: data generated by or from a cloud service provider's operations of a cloud service resulting from interactions with the cloud service customer.

3.11.3 cloud service provider data: class of data objects that are either not provided by or for the cloud service customer, or are not CSC data or cloud service derived data.

3.11.4 data portability: ability to easily transfer data from one cloud service to another without being required to re-enter data; includes cloud data portability (data between cloud services) and cloud application portability (migration of application components).

3.11.5 personally identifiable information (PII): any information that can be used to identify a natural person directly or indirectly; the person to whom PII relates is the PII principal or data subject.

3.11.6 data sharing agreement (DSA): agreement describing the terms under which data is shared between organisations, including data obligations, provenance, quality, integrity and processing restrictions.

title: Virtualisation concepts
text:
Virtualisation concepts (Clause 3.12):

3.12.1 container: isolated execution environment for running software that uses a virtualised operating system kernel (the host operating system). Software within a container is isolated and gets a controlled, limited version of the OS resources. Containers share the kernel of the host OS.

3.12.2 hypervisor (virtual machine monitor): software that virtualises physical resources, allowing multiple virtual machines to run on the underlying physical resources. A hypervisor allocates CPU, memory, disk storage and networking capabilities to each running VM.

3.12.3 serverless computing: cloud service category in which the cloud service customer can use different cloud capabilities types without having to provision, deploy and manage hardware or software resources other than providing CSC application code or CSC data. Functions as a service (FaaS) and serverless database are forms of serverless computing.

3.12.4 virtual machine (VM): isolated execution environment for running software that uses virtualised physical resources. VMs provide the functionality to execute complete software stacks including entire operating systems and application code. Multiple VMs can run on a single hardware system while remaining isolated from each other.

title: Multi-cloud and inter-cloud concepts
text:
Multi-cloud and inter-cloud concepts (Clause 3.13):

3.13.1 inter-cloud computing: cloud computing involving more than one cloud service provider where a primary CSP uses one or more cloud services provided by a secondary CSP to jointly provide cloud services to a CSC. The CSC may be unaware of the secondary CSP's involvement.

3.13.2 multi-cloud computing: cloud computing where a cloud service customer accesses cloud services directly from more than one cloud service provider. A CSC can adopt solutions that take advantage of multiple cloud services from different CSPs to achieve improved reliability, performance optimisation, best service choice and cost savings.

3.13.3 inter-cloud relationship: CSP using cloud services of other CSPs (secondary CSPs) — primary CSP takes the CSC role with secondary CSPs. CSC may be unaware of secondary CSPs.

Note: ISO/IEC 5140 provides more detail on multi-cloud and inter-cloud computing.

title: Physical organisation of cloud computing
text:
Physical organisation of cloud computing (Clause 3.14):

3.14.1 affinity: placement of two or more resources close to each other to achieve the lowest possible latency when those resources interact; resources can have low or high affinity depending on interaction frequency, criticality, bandwidth and response time requirements.

3.14.2 availability domain (availability zone): logically and physically isolated location within a cloud region; each availability domain has independent power, cooling and network infrastructure to provide fault tolerance by avoiding single points of failure. A cloud region typically has a minimum of three availability domains.

3.14.3 cloud region: geographical area containing a set of physical resources that are independent and isolated from physical resources in other cloud regions. A cloud region aims to avoid shared points of failure and provides low latency between resources within the region. Physical size is not fixed — typically large enough to survive utility failures or environmental disasters.

3.14.4 geo-dispersion: idea of not placing two resources close to each other, i.e. keeping resources separated; used for fault tolerance purposes to avoid single points of failure and for resiliency. Placing cloud service instances in multiple availability domains guards against the failure of one availability domain.

3.14.5 edge computing: distributed computing involving components existing on multiple nodes spread across a number of tiers; the edge tier has collections of nodes in distributed locations. See ISO/IEC 23188.

3.14.6 cloud service instance: entity providing the capabilities of the cloud service; each cloud service instance has its own resources, isolated from other instances, and provides a service interface for the CSC to interact with.
